post.caption: Diamonds are traded beside a train station. Antwerp, in Belgium, packs its diamond trade into about one square mile, right next to Antwerp Central Station, in an area known as the Diamond Square Mile. The first written record of the trade dates to 1447, which makes it more than five centuries old. A scaif is a polishing wheel coated in olive oil and diamond dust. In 1477, Archduke Maximilian gave Mary of Burgundy a diamond ring. Over 80 percent of the world's rough diamonds are bought in Antwerp, and more than 1,300 diamond companies employ about 3,300 people there. The city has four diamond exchanges, called bourses.
